name: Wu Chinese
sweep_summary: Wu Chinese (wuch1236) is not in the catalog. The sweep had two title hits: Lyu 2018 (UW-Madison dissertation on Ningbo prosodic phonology, 457 pp.) and Selkirk & Shen 1990 (Prosodic domains in Shanghai Chinese, in Inkelas & Zec eds.). Neither text was obtainable: Lyu 2018 is ProQuest-only (not in MINDS@UW; only a one-sentence Google Books description and the abstract/reference list of the derived article Lyu 2019, IJCHL 6(1):119-161, doi:10.1075/ijchl.19004.lyu, were readable — both are about the tone-sandhi domain = prosodic word, silent on stress placement); Selkirk & Shen 1990 exists only as an access-restricted Internet Archive lending scan (phonologysyntaxc0000unse) and a Google Books partial preview (qt0f6KuNXmkC), neither readable from our machine, and it is not on the authors' homepages. Both items are 'unclear' for word stress (prosodic-domain/tone-sandhi studies of Wu varieties), both 'no-catalog-record', priority medium. As a lead outside the item list, Duanmu 1999 (JEAL 8:1-38, doi:10.1023/A:1008353028173, paywalled; abstract saved) treats Shanghai as a moraic-/disyllabic-trochee system where 'the initial syllable determines the tonal pattern of a multisyllabic domain' — the likeliest first-hand stress source for Shanghai Wu, but no page-located stress statement was read, so best_new_statement is found=false.org metadata and publisher pages.

sources.quote: This dissertation will investigate the prosodic phonology of the Ningbo dialect under the framework of the theory of prosodic phonology. [Google Books record] — Lyu 2019 abstract: "It will show that the lexical tone sandhi rule (LTS) applies within the domain formed by the major types of morpho-syntactic words in Ningbo dialect. However, pure phonological information may also affect the application of LTS."
sources.locator: Google Books catalogue description (one sentence); Lyu 2019 abstract page (John Benjamins)
sources.note: Nothing on word-stress placement is reachable. The dissertation is a Nespor-Vogel-style prosodic-hierarchy study of Ningbo (Northern Wu) whose visible content (Google Books description; the 2019 IJCHL article derived from it, keywords 'minimal word requirement', 'prosodic word', 'tone sandhi'; reference list citing Duanmu 1993 'Rime length, stress, and association domains' and Duanmu 1999) concerns the tone-sandhi domain = prosodic word. Whether it makes an explicit claim about metrical prominence/stress in Ningbo words cannot be judged without the text. Full text is on ProQuest only (not in…

sources.note: Not read. Title and venue indicate an analysis of the prosodic domains (prosodic word / phonological phrase) governing Shanghai tone sandhi, i.e. prosody of a Wu variety but not necessarily a word-stress statement. The Internet Archive scan is lending-only (search-inside returns 'Item not available'), Google Books serves only a partial preview whose page images are not delivered to this host, and the chapter is not on Selkirk's UMass page (people.umass.edu/selkirk/pdf/) or Inkelas's Berkeley publications page. Semantic Scholar/OpenAlex/Crossref record no DOI or open copy.
